commands.name: agent-reach
commands.description:

commands.name: docx
commands.description: Use this skill whenever the user wants to create, read, edit, or manipulate Word documents (.docx files) or Word templates (.dotx files). Triggers include: any mention of 'Word doc', 'word document', '.docx', '.dotx', or requests to produce professional documents with formatting like tables of contents, headings, page numbers, or letterheads. Also use when extracting or reorganizing content from .docx or .dotx files, inserting or replacing images in documents, performing find-and-replace in Word files, working with tracked changes or comments, or converting content into a polished Word document. If the user asks for a 'report', 'memo', 'letter', 'template', or similar deliverable as a Word or .docx file, use this skill. Do NOT use for PDFs, spreadsheets, Google Docs, or general coding tasks unrelated to document generation. (user)

commands.name: mcp-builder
commands.description: Guide for creating high-quality MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers that enable LLMs to interact with external services through well-designed tools. Use when building MCP servers to integrate external APIs or services, whether in Python (FastMCP) or Node/TypeScript (MCP SDK). (user)

commands.name: morning
commands.description: Render the user's morning brief as a styled HTML artifact, or set it up as a recurring weekday task. Use only when the user explicitly asks to run, see, or set up their morning brief, or if they invoke /morning by name. A question about their day, schedule, or calendar is not by itself a request for the brief; answer it directly instead. (user)

commands.name: pdf
commands.description: Use this skill whenever the user wants to do anything with PDF files. This includes reading or extracting text/tables from PDFs, combining or merging multiple PDFs into one, splitting PDFs apart, rotating pages, adding watermarks, creating new PDFs, filling PDF forms, encrypting/decrypting PDFs, extracting images, and OCR on scanned PDFs to make them searchable. If the user mentions a .pdf file or asks to produce one, use this skill. (user)

commands.name: pptx
commands.description: Use this skill any time a .pptx or .potx file is involved in any way — as input, output, or both. This includes: creating slide decks, pitch decks, or presentations; reading, parsing, or extracting text from any .pptx or .potx file (even if the extracted content will be used elsewhere, like in an email or summary); editing, modifying, or updating existing presentations; combining or splitting slide files; working with templates (.potx), layouts, speaker notes, or comments. Trigger whenever the user mentions "deck," "slides," "presentation," or references a .pptx or .potx filename, regardless of what they plan to do with the content afterward. If a .pptx or .potx file needs to be opened, created, or touched, use this skill. (user)

commands.name: startup-hook-skill

commands.name: xlsx
commands.description: Use this skill any time a spreadsheet file is the primary input or output. This means any task where the user wants to: open, read, edit, or fix an existing .xlsx, .xlsm, .xltx, .csv, or .tsv file (e.g., adding columns, computing formulas, formatting, charting, cleaning messy data); create a new spreadsheet from scratch or from other data sources; or convert between tabular file formats. Trigger especially when the user references a spreadsheet file by name or path — even casually (like "the xlsx in my downloads") — and wants something done to it or produced from it. commands.name: design-sync

commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

commands.name: update-config
commands.description: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. 230	    const degradedModeRate = this.totalCalls > 0
231	      ? this.degradedCalls / this.totalCalls
232	      : 0;
233	
234	    // Get audit trail stats for additional metrics
235	    let auditStats = {
236	      blockRate: 0,
237	      avgRiskScore: 0,
238	      totalEvents: 0,
239	    };
240	    try {
241	      const { getAuditTrailStats } = await import('../governance/audit-trail-persistence');
242	      const stats = await getAuditTrailStats(3600000); // Last 1 hour
243	      auditStats = {
244	        blockRate: stats.blockRate,
245	        avgRiskScore: stats.avgRiskScore,
246	        totalEvents: stats.totalEvents,
247	      };
248	    } catch (err) {
249	      // Non-blocking: continue with default values
250	    }
251	
252	    // Calculate fallback rate
253	    const fallbackRate = this.totalCalls > 0
254	      ? (this.degradedCalls / this.totalCalls) * 100
255	      : 0;
256	
257	    // Circuit breaker trip count
258	    const circuitBreakerTripCount = circuitBreakerMetrics.reduce(
259	      (sum, m) => sum + (m.failures || 0),
260	      0
261	    );
262	
263	    return {
264	      status: overallHealth,
265	      subsystems: {
266	        nervousSystem: {
267	          status: overallHealth,
268	          totalCalls: this.totalCalls,
269	          successfulCalls: this.successfulCalls,
270	          degradedCalls: this.degradedCalls,
271	        },
272	        circuitBreakers: {
273	          status: circuitBreakerHealth,
274	          openCount: openBreakers,
275	          totalBreakers: circuitBreakerMetrics.length,
276	          tripCount: circuitBreakerTripCount,
277	          metrics: circuitBreakerMetrics,
278	        },
279	        rateLimiter: {
280	          status: rateLimiterHealth,
281	          utilization: rateLimitUtilization,
282	          stats: rateLimitStats,
283	        },
284	      },
285	      metrics: {
286	        totalCalls: this.totalCalls,
287	        successRate: Math.round(successRate * 100) / 100,
288	        averageLatency: Math.round(avgLatency),
289	        degradedModeRate: Math.round(degradedModeRate * 100) / 100,
290	        fallbackRate: Math.round(fallbackRate * 10) / 10,
291	        blockRate: Math.round(auditStats.blockRate * 10) / 10,
292	        avgRiskScore: auditStats.avgRiskScore,
293	        circuitBreakerTripCount,
294	        rateLimitUtilization: Math.round(rateLimitUtilization * 100) / 100,
295	      },
296	      diagnostics: {
297	        circuitBreakerState: circuitBreakerMetrics[0]?.state || 'CLOSED',
298	        auditTrailEvents: auditStats.totalEvents,
299	        latencySamples: this.latencies.length,
300	      },
301	      timestamp: Date.now(),
302	    };
303	  }

295	    CONFIG.WINDOW_MS = updates.windowMs;
296	  }
297	
298	  log.info(`Rate limit config updated:`, CONFIG);
299	}
300	
301	// ============================================================================
302	// EXPORTS
303	// ============================================================================
304	
305	export const InternalRateLimiter = {
306	  checkRateLimit,
307	  recordGovernanceCall,
308	  getRateLimitStats,
309	  getCorrelationStats,
310	  getPerCorrelationSaturation,
311	  resetRateLimits,

Done. The fix is in `server/nervous-system/integrated-nervous-system.ts`.

**Root cause:** `NervousSystemHealth` had drifted away from what `getHealth()` actually returns. The interface described `subsystems` as four bare status strings and put `circuitBreakerState` inside `metrics`, while the implementation returns per-subsystem detail objects and a separate `diagnostics` block. A stale `@ts-ignore` on the `rateLimiter` line was masking the `subsystems` half of the mismatch, leaving only the `metrics.circuitBreakerState` error (TS2741) visible.

**What I changed:**
- Rewrote `NervousSystemHealth` to match the real return shape: `subsystems.{nervousSystem, circuitBreakers, rateLimiter}` as objects with a `status` plus their supporting counters, and a `diagnostics` block holding `circuitBreakerState`, `auditTrailEvents`, `latencySamples`.
- Typed the nested payloads against their real sources rather than restating them: `CircuitBreakerMetrics[]` (type-only import from `../governance/circuit-breaker`) and `ReturnType<typeof InternalRateLimiter.getRateLimitStats>`, so future drift in those modules surfaces here.
- Extracted the repeated `'healthy' | 'degraded' | 'critical'` union into an exported `HealthStatus` alias.
- Removed the now-unnecessary `@ts-ignore` at the old line 257 — the implementation type-checks against the corrected interface.

No suppressions, casts, or deleted logic; the runtime behavior of `getHealth()` is untouched.

**Verification caveat:** I could not run `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` — every compiler invocation I tried (`npx tsc`, `./node_modules/.bin/tsc`, `node node_modules/typescript/bin/tsc`, `npm run check`) and the serena diagnostics tool came back "requires approval". So the check is unrun on my side. What I did verify by inspection: every property in the returned literal has a matching field of the right type, and no file outside this one reads the fields I moved or renamed — I grepped the whole repo for `circuitBreakerState`, `subsystems.circuitBreaker`, `subsystems.curiosityEngine`, `subsystems.shadowMode`, and `NervousSystemHealth`; the only consumers (`server/api/mcp-governance-health.ts:88-90,349-352` and `getHealthWithAlerts` in this file) use only fields I kept. If you approve the typecheck command I'll run it and confirm.

One pre-existing issue I did **not** touch, since it's outside this task: `integrated-nervous-system-e2e.test.ts:163,172,194,510` reads `health.metrics.degradedRate`, which the implementation has never returned (it returns `degradedModeRate`). That was already an error before my change and still is.
